properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 25 at 9:11AM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday during high tides.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur in the
morning hours.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents in the warned area should
be alert for rising water and take appropriate action to protect
life and property. High tides each day will occur in the
morning. Tides may be anywhere from 1 to 1.7 feet above
astronomical tide predictions.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth. Stay off of jetties and sea walls. Avoid
beaches during high tides. During high and rising tides, waves
may run farther up the beach than expected. Stay far back from the
water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 10:07AM MDT until October 27 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Catastrophic flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Major flooding along San Juan River is occurring or
expected to begin shortly.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1002 AM MDT, At 9:30 AM MDT Sunday the stage was 19.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 43.6 feet early Monday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage early Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 32.0
feet on 09/10/1927.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Tselakai Dezza, Bluff, Halchita, Montezuma Creek and
Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 9:06AM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...From 9 AM Monday to 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
11:39 AM Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at
12:15 PM Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at
12:56 PM Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft
MLLW) at 01:43 PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up
to 1.0 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts near 30 kt.

the Suwannee River out 60 NM.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EDT /1 PM CDT/ Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20

properties.areaDesc: Rio Arriba, NM
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 8:26AM MDT until October 26 at 10:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 AM MDT Sunday the stage was 6.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:00 AM MDT Sunday was 8.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river will recede slightly to 6.2 feet this
afternoon. It will then rise to 7.0 feet just after midnight
tonight. It will fall below flood stage late tomorrow morning to
4.3 feet Thursday evening then rise again.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.0
feet on 05/17/1993.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Monday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Sandoval, NM
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 8:22AM MDT until October 26 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Jemez River Above Jemez Pueblo affecting Sandoval County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Jemez River above Jemez Pueblo.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Between 7 and 8 feet multiple locations
along highway 4 between San Ysidro and Jemez Springs will see water
crossing the road from tributaries and low water crossing points.
The Wastewater Treatment plant 1 mile downstream of Jemez Springs
can be impacted between 7 and 7.7 feet. Water will be on Highway 4
at mile marker 1, 2 and 13.  Homes near the river in San Ysidro
could be impacted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM MDT Sunday the stage was 5.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.5 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Action stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Monday afternoon at noon MDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande  at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From late tonight to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 9.2 feet tomorrow morning.
It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.3
feet on 05/18/1944.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.
